$comment: Tier-3 (DB-state) spec for v4's EMBEDDING_REFIT handler (W4.7e2 — the BUILTIN
TF-IDF embedder refit). One committed file drives BOTH sides:
- the v4 oracle (build-embedding-refit-fixture.ts + embedding-refit-tier3.ts)
- the Rust port (quilltap-harness embedding_refit_tier3 equivalence test).
WHAT IT PROVES: handleEmbeddingRefit gathers every character's memories
fitCorpus's the BUILTIN vocabulary, persists it via tfidf_vocabularies.
upsertByProfileId, and enqueues EMBEDDING_REINDEX_ALL (priority -1). The
differential diffs tfidf_vocabularies + background_jobs.
FIXTURE: two DBs (main + mount-index). Characters are baked via v4's REAL
repos.characters.create (minted ids + vaults); memories reference the minted
character ids by name; the BUILTIN embedding profile has a PINNED id so both
sides build the job with a known profileId. Both sides read a COPY of this
SAME baked fixture, then run the handler; the READS see identical ids, the
WRITES (the vocab row + the reindex job) mint fresh ids/timestamps that are
placeholder-normalized.
NORMALIZATION: id/createdAt/updatedAt (both tables) + scheduledAt (jobs) are
placeholdered; fittedAt is PINNED (the injected fit clock == v4's frozen Date).
The idf column carries the Math.log libm seam (macOS ln vs V8 Math.log differ
by <=1 ULP) — its JSON array is compared NUMERICALLY at 1e-12, everything else
byte-exact. Corpus/vocabulary order is mathematically irrelevant (set+sort, df
counts, sum/count avg), so cross-side iteration order cannot diverge the output.
SAFETY: testPepperBase64 is a THROWAWAY 32-byte key (shared with the other
tier-2 fixtures); it protects nothing real.
